Class HttpResponse

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.net.HttpResponse
public final class HttpResponse extends Object
An immutable snapshot of one HttpClient/HttpsClient response: status, body/headers (the caller-owned buffers passed into the request call), and bodyLength/headersLength (the number of bytes actually written into each, truncated to the buffer's own length if the response was longer). status is the HTTP status code (e.g. 200), or 0 if the connection failed before a status line was received.

A fresh instance is constructed on every request — cheap, since it only holds three ints and two array references, never a copy of the buffers themselves. Juno's arena never frees memory, so a caller looping forever (like MadridWeather) should still keep body/headers themselves allocated once outside the loop and pass the same buffers into every call; only this small wrapper is allocated per call. juno inspect --risks estimates how many iterations that budget allows.
